answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay. Each agent must lock a bond to join the garden of services, and its voting weight grows only from sustained, verified work, not from spawning copies. A lone sparrow that behaves honestly accumulates trust slowly, while a clone farm pays the same bond per identity and gains nothing extra, since weight depends on history, not headcount. Periodic re-attestation caps old reputation, so attackers reaching the summit of influence must keep paying real costs instead of coasting on a one-time flood of fake identities.
